judge.reasoning: The answer accurately explains and provides the formula showing that MultiHead(Q, K, V) is computed using Concat to combine the individual attention heads.

rows.answer:
Multi-head attention is computed by concatenating the attention heads and then projecting them using a parameter matrix $W^O$:

$$\text{MultiHead}(Q, K, V) = \text{Concat}(\text{head}_1, ..., \text{head}_h)W^O$$
where each head is computed as:
$$\text{head}_i = \text{Attention}(QW_i^Q, KW_i^K, VW_i^V)$$

In these equations, the projections are parameter matrices:
- $W_i^Q \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_k}$
- $W_i^K \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_k}$
- $W_i^V \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_v}$
- $W^O \in \mathbb{R}^{h d_v \times d_{\text{model}}}$

The system answer clearly and accurately states that the late-interaction operator is computed using the maximum dot product, providing both a verbal explanation and the exact mathematical formula.

rows.answer:
The late-interaction operator $\text{LI}(q, d)$ is computed as the sum over all query token embedding vectors $\mathbf{E}_q^{(i)}$ of their maximum dot product with each of the document token embedding vectors $\mathbf{E}_d^{(j)}$. Formally, the formula is:

$$\text{LI}(q, d) = \sum_{i \in [1, N_q]} \max_{j \in [1, N_d]} \langle \mathbf{E}_q^{(i)} | \mathbf{E}_d^{(j)} \rangle$$

where $N_q$ and $N_d$ are the number of vectors in the query and document page embeddings, respectively, and $\langle \cdot | \cdot \rangle$ denotes the dot product.
